findings.reason: The diff deletes `if (opts.flowSkipColonSpace) opts.quoteFlowKeys = true` in createPresenterState. presenter.ts:215/223 then writes `key:value` with an empty separator, and parser.ts:807-809 only ends a plain scalar at ':' when whitespace or a flow indicator follows, so `a:1` is read as one key. Severity is high, between C1's critical and X1's high: the corruption is silent, but it only happens when the opt-in option is set.
findings.claim: Removing the forced quoteFlowKeys when flowSkipColonSpace is set makes dump() emit `{a:1}`, which this repo's loader reads back as {"a:1": null}, silently corrupting data on round trip.
findings.evidence: The diff deletes `if (opts.flowSkipColonSpace) { opts.quoteFlowKeys = true }` from createPresenterState. writeFlowMapping (presenter.ts:215,223) then writes `${keyText}:${sep}${valueText}` with sep = '' and a plain, unquoted key. The plain-scalar reader in src/parser/parser.ts:807-809 stops at ':' only when the next character is whitespace or a flow indicator (`if (isWsOrEolOrEnd(following) || (inFlow && isFlowIndicator(following))) break`). So in `{a:1}` the colon is read as part of the scalar `a:1`, not as a key/value separator. The removed doc text said exactly this: "otherwise `a:1` would be parsed as a single plain scalar instead of a mapping entry". CHANGELOG.md:302 records the same fix in the predecessor option (3.10.0: "Fix `condenseFlow` output (quote keys for sure, instead of spaces), #371"), and docs/migrate_v4_to_v5.md:184 sends `condenseFlow` users to this option. Any scalar value is affected (numbers, strings, booleans); only values starting with `{` or `[` still split correctly.

findings.reason: dump-options.test.mjs:154 only does assert.equal on the dumped string. The quoteFlowKeys test at :162 does load the output back. The only round-trip property test, dump-fuzzy.test.mjs:36, is it.skip, so nothing in the suite catches the C1/X1 break.
findings.claim: The flowSkipColonSpace test only checks the output string `{a:1}` and never loads it back, so the round-trip break goes uncaught.
findings.evidence: Line 154: `assert.equal(dump({ a: 1 }, { flowLevel: 0, flowSkipColonSpace: true }), '{a:1}\n')`, with no `load(output)` check. The quoteFlowKeys test two blocks below does run `assert.deepEqual(load(output), { [key]: 1 })`. The only round-trip property test that varies `flowSkipColonSpace` is disabled: test/core/dump-fuzzy.test.mjs:36 uses `it.skip('Load from dumped should be the original object', ...)`.
